question: Does combining the cheap integer-slot ceiling with the quartet flag avoid more graph fallbacks than either alone?
domain: All 384480 retained certified cell/order/budget queries, without filtering. Six fixed budgets and 64080 queries per budget.
routes: union of factor4 and quartet admission
comparison: All routes share beta rejection and final exact graph decisions. Union admits if either established sufficient admission check admits; it never modifies endpoints, budgets or rankings.
metrics: union graph reduction vs factor4, including zero budgets and no-gain budgets
validation: Join by exact case/fraction keys; assert identical final decisions for all inputs. Assert every scalar admit has exact admit; union has no fewer admissions than either constituent and no more than full-factor scalar admission.
scope: Finite dependent declared-model questions; neither measured runtime nor a physical accuracy/choice gain. The compound sufficient route is a local posthoc analysis of existing frozen route records, not newly collected data. Do not equate scalar/graph counts with CPU time; full-factor exponential preprocessing and polynomial quartet classification are different costs.
